Thanks for the ping and the logs. Initial read: the symptoms look consistent with queue saturation in the streaming workers + excessive small writes from the client side (load pattern producing many tiny frames). Two hypotheses to prioritize:

1) Batch queue starvation / head-of-line blocking when many concurrent SSE streams have active KV cache misses — causing per-token latency spikes for a small subset of requests, which would raise p99 without changing p95 much.
2) Backpressure misconfiguration between the streaming proxy and model workers — sudden connection bursts cause buffer queues to grow and the worker scheduler to favor longer-running requests, creating stalls on short requests.

Data we need right away (please provide):
- per-second connection count for the Finexa API key (past 48h)
- histogram of model token latency (p50/p95/p99) by minute for past 6h
- streaming worker queue length / backlog metrics by host for past 2h
- any GC/pause events on the workers during the spike window

Immediate mitigation options we can attempt (low-risk first):
- Enable per-key burst throttling to smooth arrival rate (config at gateway) — low-risk and reversible.
- Temporarily route Finexa to a dedicated smaller model variant or to dedicated capacity (if they have reserved we can flip) — needs ops approval.
- Short-term: lower streaming write buffer and enable prefix cache TTL increase to reduce KV misses.

I'm attaching the prod_playbook.txt with checklist for streaming incidents. I'll start pulling metrics and post updates in INF-4212.

— Marcus

Subject: Finexa incident recap & action items — streaming p99 regression (resolved -> mitigation in place)

Summary of the incident and current state (post-mitigation):
- Timeline: first customer report 2026-03-07 15:22 PST; mitigation live 2026-03-09 12:10 PST; follow-up checks completed 2026-03-09 17:45 PST.
- Symptom: SSE/WebSocket p99 jumps to ~8–12s during peak; error-rate transiently ~1.8%. p95 largely stable.
- Root cause (preliminary): streaming worker queue backlog + per-connection write contention exposing KV cache miss latencies for a small subset of streams. Full RCA in progress (INF-4212).

Actions taken:
1) Immediate: Enabled per-key burst smoothing at gateway for Finexa and routed 20% of traffic to polling fallback for 6 hours (reduced error-rate to baseline within 40 mins).
2) Capacity: Spun ephemeral additional streaming pool nodes in us-east for 48 hours (ops confirmed, no SLA exposure).
3) Engineering mitigations: decreased streaming write buffer and raised prefix cache TTL for affected model; implementing scheduler patch to reduce head-of-line blocking (in review).
4) Customer care: offered $5k credit and 8 hours of dedicated engineering troubleshooting time (accepted in principle).

Open items / owners:
- Clean RCA writeup with sequence diagrams (Marcus) — target: 2026-03-11 17:00 PST.
- Post-mortem perf test reproducing 3k concurrent SSE streams & validation of scheduler patch (Marcus + Performance team) — target: 2026-03-13.
- Finalize customer concession and Handoff to AM (Sean/Evelyn) — target: 2026-03-10.

Attachments included in thread: sso snapshot (slo_snapshot.csv), prod_playbook.txt, error_snapshots.zip.
